solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seeking independence in process of interrogation

parts.note: a quest is a seeking or search
I is a standard abbreviation for independence or independent
on means under way, in progress, as in 'the work is on'

explanation.surface: A detainee's quest for freedom while being grilled by interrogators.
explanation.definitionFit: A question is an act of asking, and interrogation is formal asking, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: Put an end to heartless monarch at church

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for the monarch is removed

parts.note: a queen is a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone ends the reign of a cruel ruler while at church.
explanation.definitionFit: To quench a fire or thirst is to put a stop to it, an exact verb synonym.

clue.text: Zebra, for example, is one of five in Eastern Spain

indicators.note: in places the quintuplet word between the two E letters

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together

explanation.surface: A zoo-like picture: a zebra, one of five animals, found in eastern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The zebra belongs to the horse family, so it is an example of a horse-like animal, an equid.

clue.text: Archbishop's cut short twice by expression of disapproval

indicators.note: twice means the shortened name is written two times
cut short means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Desmond Tutu was Archbishop of Cape Town

explanation.surface: A famous archbishop interrupted by someone clicking their tongue at him.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Archbishop is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is the tongue-click sound people make when they disapprove of something.

clue.text: Strange presence in part of Bible that everybody knows

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, one part of the Bible

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of presence are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spooky presence lurking in a passage of scripture that everyone already knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like it describes the presence but signals the anagram; 'part of Bible' is the Old Testament abbreviation, the usual crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is a supposedly confidential matter that is in fact common knowledge.

clue.text: Anger ahead of time for card game

indicators.note: ahead of puts the word for anger in front of the time abbreviation

parts.note: pique is resentment or irritation

explanation.surface: Someone losing their temper just before it is time for a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Piquet is an old two-player card game played with a short pack of 32 cards.

clue.text: Short of cash after misfortune, with one pound

parts.note: ill can mean harm or misfortune, as in 'ill befell him'
I is the Roman numeral for one
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone broke after bad luck, left with just a single pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiquid describes a person or firm lacking ready money, assets not easily turned into cash.

clue.text: Anxieties still among us in Berlin

indicators.note: among puts the word for still inside the German word

parts.note: uns is German for us, as spoken in Berlin
still means quiet, calm

explanation.surface: Lingering worries persist among a group of people in Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unquiets, as a noun, are states of unrest or disquiet, that is worries.

clue.text: Sickness with no date recorded in ancient city

indicators.note: recorded in means written inside, so the abbreviation is set within the city's name

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city of Egypt and also of Greece
ND is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: An illness noted in the annals of an ancient city, with no date given.
explanation.definitionFit: The bends is decompression sickness suffered by divers who surface too fast.

clue.text: Shares supply with associates short of phosphorus

indicators.note: short of means the element's symbol is removed from the supply word

parts.note: to equip is to supply or furnish
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
ties are links or associations

explanation.surface: A trading story: shares provided to partners, but a chemical is lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Equities are ordinary stocks in a company, the stock-market sense of shares.

clue.text: Hired audience of 100 need to be heard

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: to be heard signals that the word for need is said aloud, not spelt

parts.note: lack means need or want

explanation.surface: A hundred people need to make themselves heard, like an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A claque is a group paid to applaud at a performance, historically in French theatres.

clue.text: Criminal who is French avoids international capture

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal

indicators.note: avoids means the abbreviation is left out of the French words

parts.note: qui est is French for who is

explanation.surface: A French criminal dodges an international arrest warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is the act of seizing or taking by force, so a capture.

clue.text: Team making joke about European drug? On the contrary

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round another
on the contrary flips which goes round which, so the letters for European and drug surround the joke

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A team cracking jokes about a European drug, or is it the other way round?
explanation.definitionFit: Equipe is a French word for team, borrowed in English especially for motor-racing or sports teams.

clue.text: Mass with Latin and tuna oil substituted

parts.note: cum is the Latin word for with

indicators.note: substituted signals the letters of tuna oil are replaced by a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe swap: a mass said in Latin, with tuna oil put in instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service but is a heap; 'substituted' turns TUNA OIL into ULATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A cumulation is an accumulated heap or pile, so a mass of things.

clue.text: Informed expert about charmingly old-fashioned duke

indicators.note: about means the expert word goes round the old-fashioned word

parts.note: an ace is an expert
quaint means attractively old-fashioned

explanation.surface: An expert gives a quaint old duke the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acquainted with something is to know of it, to have been told, so informed.

clue.text: Cavalry corps function before plundering cities, ultimately

indicators.note: before puts the function abbreviation in front

parts.note: cos is the abbreviation for cosine, a trigonometric function
sack means plundering, as in the sack of a city

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of cities

explanation.surface: Horsemen whose job was to ride in ahead of the looting of cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were frontier horsemen famous as light cavalry in the Russian army.

clue.text: Lovely place in France where you can see old cars

definitions.text: where you can see old cars

parts.note: beau is French for lovely or beautiful
lieu is French for place

explanation.surface: A beautiful French spot that happens to have a vintage-car display.
explanation.walkthrough: Beaulieu is a village in Hampshire, England, home of the National Motor Museum; 'in France' supplies the French words.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaulieu houses Britain's National Motor Museum, full of veteran and vintage vehicles.

clue.text: Trips escort arranged around Oxford University

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the university abbreviation
arranged signals the letters of escort are reordered

explanation.surface: A guide organises outings around the Oxford colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-tours are holidays or excursions to natural areas planned to limit environmental harm.

clue.text: Turbulent epoch, with Queen being one that is not crossed

indicators.note: turbulent signals the letters of epoch and Queen are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A stormy era in which a queen proved one nobody dared cross.
explanation.walkthrough: A British cheque is crossed with two lines to make it payable only into a bank account; an uncrossed one can be cashed over the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: An open cheque is a bank order to pay that lacks the two parallel lines restricting payment.

clue.text: Former president to the French will have no hesitation making capital

indicators.note: will have no means the hesitation sound is dropped from the president's name

parts.note: Gamal Abdel Nasser was a former president of Egypt
er is a sound of hesitation
au is French for to the

explanation.surface: An ex-president speaking French decisively, without hesitating, about a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Strange about Burmese man's title being one in file

indicators.note: about means the strange word goes round the Burmese title

parts.note: queer means strange or odd
U is a Burmese honorific for a man, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: An odd tale about a Burmese man's title placed in a file.
explanation.definitionFit: A queuer is someone waiting in a line, and a file is a line of people one behind another.

clue.text: They're of greater importance though they shouldn't be heard

definitions.meaning: the main sides of old pop singles, the tracks promoted as more important than the flip side
stage remarks spoken to the audience that the other characters supposedly do not hear

explanation.surface: Records' main sides matter more, yet remarks muttered apart are meant to go unheard.
explanation.definitionFit: A-sides were the featured tracks of singles; asides are stage remarks meant only for the audience.

clue.text: Couple of pints on board — there'll be no river exercises

indicators.note: on board means within a ship, so the shortened measure goes inside

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the board one is on

indicators.note: there'll be no means the river abbreviation is removed from the measure

parts.note: a quart is two pints

explanation.surface: Sailors with a couple of pints aboard and no river: time for some exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Squats are exercises in which you crouch with bent knees and stand up again.

clue.text: Monkeys about in brands — not right

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for about inside the shortened brands word
not means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: marques are brands, especially of cars
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Monkeys messing about among brand names, not quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaques are a genus of Old World monkeys, including the rhesus and Barbary apes.

clue.text: Exclusive drink with no alternative in Cyprus

indicators.note: in puts the shortened drink inside the Cyprus code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus

indicators.note: with no means the word for alternative is removed from the drink

parts.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: An exclusive drinks party in Cyprus offering no choice of tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliquy describes a group that keeps to itself and shuts others out, like a clique.

clue.text: This converted vehicle is used by assassins

indicators.note: converted signals the letters of this are changed into a new order

parts.note: a quad is a four-wheeled motorbike, a vehicle

explanation.surface: A modified vehicle that a gang of killers drives around in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit squad is a group of killers sent to murder someone, so a team of assassins.

clue.text: Fruit to squeeze?

definitions.meaning: the gourd family produces marrows and pumpkins, botanically fruits
to press or crush something flat

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether fruit is meant to be pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A squash is a gourd fruit like a marrow, and to squash is to crush flat.

clue.text: Asks for space for lots of paper

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A clerk requests room for a big pile of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To enquire is to ask a question, so the verb forms match.
